text: SYNA's fundamentals don't match the momentum: four straight quarters of operating losses with margins stuck between -2.8% and -8.1%, and insiders have sold $5.2M with zero buys in six months. speaker: GPT-OSS
text: If you try to buy an Indian IPO with only Rs 10 000, you’ll almost certainly get nothing – most IPOs require a full lot of 200 shares, and the allotment process is a lottery. Even if you hit the lottery, the lock‑up period is 90 days and the expected value after that is tiny once you factor in the 0.38 % round‑trip cost and 20 % short‑term CGT if you sell early. For a Reliance.NS purchase on Zerodha delivery, you’ll pay zero brokerage, but you’ll incur STT 0.5 %, exchange fee 0.59 %, SEBI 0.02 %, stamp duty 1.5 %, GST 0.11 % and a DP charge of Rs 15.93 per share per day you hold. On a Rs 10 000 position that’s about Rs 38 total, or 0.38 % of the trade. If you hold for a year you’ll get the 12.5 % long‑term CGT exemption up to Rs 1.25 lakh, so the tax bite is minimal after that. As for cars and battery names, the big auto stocks (Tata Motors TS, Maruti SUV, Mahindra M) and battery makers (Exide EXI, Amara‑Vistas AMV) all trade above Rs 400, so with Rs 10 000 you’d own only a handful of shares and the 0.38 % cost would eat most of a 1–2 % move.
